item.research_question: How does the sintering temperature (1200–1400 °C) during spark plasma sintering of mechanically alloyed CrMoNbWV powders affect the microstructure evolution, phase formation, and resulting mechanical, wear, and corrosion properties?
item.material_system: Equiatomic CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) synthesized from elemental Nb, Mo, W, V, and Cr powders (99.9% purity) with ~3.5 wt.% Fe contamination from milling balls.
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying (MA) for 5 h in a planetary mill (Fritsch Pulverisette 4) at 350/700 rpm in Ar atmosphere, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) in a graphite die (Ø40 mm) at 1200, 1300, and 1400 °C under 50 MPa pressure for 5 min.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compressive testing on cylindrical specimens (12 mm height, 6 mm diameter); abrasive wear tests per ASTM G65 using silica sand (212–300 µm) at 130 N load; electrochemical corrosion tests in 0.5 M H2SO4 at room temperature using Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
key_findings: MA powders formed a single-phase BCC solid solution with lattice parameter a = 3.146 Å, containing 3.5 wt.% Fe from milling balls.
SPS at 1200 °C resulted in 41.6 vol.% Laves phases (Cr2Nb, (Fe,Cr)Nb) and 4.7 vol.% oxides (NbVO4–VO); Laves phase content decreased to 21.5 vol.% at 1300 °C and 11.5 vol.% at 1400 °C.
Compressive strength of all sintered samples ranged from 2700 to 2870 MPa, with low plasticity attributed to brittle Laves phases and oxides at grain boundaries.
Bulk loss of the carburized surface layer was 0.001 cm³, which was lower than nickel-bonded tungsten carbide (0.003 cm³); after removing the layer, bulk loss increased to 0.0035–0.0048 cm³.
Corrosion current density (i_corr) in 0.5 M H2SO4 was 2.81 µA/cm² (1200 °C), 0.20 µA/cm² (1300 °C), and 0.88 µA/cm² (1400 °C), indicating best corrosion resistance at 1300 °C.
Carburized layer thickness ranged from 18 to 75 µm, increasing with sintering temperature due to carbon diffusion from the graphite die.
The alloy density was calculated as 10.55 g/cm³, which is lower than the WNbMoTaV alloy (12.42 g/cm³) while maintaining comparable mechanical and corrosive properties.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the initial BCC formation to high mixing entropy and low valence electron concentration (VEC = 5.6). Laves phase precipitation during SPS is explained by the smaller atomic radius of Cr compared to Nb, reducing elastic energy and consistent with the Nb-Cr-Fe phase diagram. Oxide formation is linked to high oxygen affinity of Nb and V. Increased sintering temperature promotes reverse dissolution of Laves phases due to the dominant entropy component (ΔS_mix) over enthalpy (ΔH_mix) and enhanced diffusion. Low plasticity results from brittle Laves phases and oxides acting as crack initiation sites at grain boundaries, while coarse oxides at 1400 °C further reduce ductility. High strength is attributed to grain boundary hardening (Hall–Petch), solid solution hardening (substitutional and interstitial O/C), and precipitation hardening by Laves phases and oxides.
item.limitations: The authors state that the samples exhibit low plasticity due to the high volume fraction of brittle Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries. Additionally, the presence of Fe impurities (3.5 wt.%) from milling balls and unavoidable oxygen contamination during MA and SPS led to oxide formation and carburization, which may affect the intrinsic properties of the alloy.
item.future_work: The authors propose that further research will be aimed at obtaining a powder without iron, studying the effect of SPS process duration, and investigating additional post-process heat treatment on the alloy's structure and properties.
quotes: The MA powders' phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution.
The sintered samples exhibit the compressive strength of 2700–2870 MPa.
